message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on North Carolina Avenue in this Monopoly auction.

I have $726 and four houses on the dark blues. Gemini has almost no cash and owns dangerous dark blues. GPT has $763 but is in jail with mortgaged light blues.

The current bid is $87. I should raise to the minimum $88. I will cap my bid at $150. That lets me mortgage North Carolina Avenue back for cash if I win. It also prevents GPT from completing a Pacific Avenue and North Carolina Avenue pair.

I realized blocking GPT from North Carolina Avenue does not actually prevent a green monopoly. Pacific Avenue is mortgaged and owned by Gemini, so GPT cannot complete the greens even with Pennsylvania Avenue. My prior reasoning was flawed.

Bidding $88 nets $62 cash after mortgaging. Up to $149 is profitable. At $150 the net is zero. Above that it loses money.

Unmortgaging North Carolina Avenue would cost $165, so it is not worth doing without a green monopoly. The mortgage value remains the only practical return. I will continue bidding up to the $150 cap and drop if GPT raises past it.

Selling all twelve pink houses would raise $600. Combined with cash, that gives $1326 total liquid assets. Boardwalk at four houses costs $1700, so I cannot afford it even after selling all houses. Park Place with three houses costs $1100, which is within reach.

Winning at $88 leaves me with $788 cash after mortgaging. If GPT wins instead, they would end up around $825 either way. Each extra dollar I bid forces them to pay more. I am now weighing whether to push the bid above the $150 cap just to bleed their cash.

I will not push the bid above $150. If GPT raises past that cap, I will drop and let them pay $150 to mortgage back for a net zero cash return. Bidding higher risks overpaying or losing the auction outright.

I now see the real danger. If GPT wins North Carolina Avenue, they would own Pennsylvania Avenue and North Carolina Avenue together. They could trade with Gemini for Pacific Avenue to complete a green monopoly. Gemini is nearly broke and owns the dark blues, so he might trade Pacific to GPT for cash or help. That would give GPT a dangerous green monopoly.

Gemini cannot build more houses because all houses are already placed. He has no cash to unmortgage properties either. This makes a trade for Pacific Avenue unlikely. If I own North Carolina Avenue, GPT would need to deal with me directly to assemble the green monopoly.

The blocking value of owning North Carolina Avenue is significant beyond the $150 mortgage. A green monopoly would be dangerous, but no houses remain to build on. Unimproved greens rent only $52 each, so the immediate threat is limited. I am now checking which players have houses that could be sold back.

All 32 houses are on the board. No new houses can be placed until someone sells back existing ones. The blocking value of owning North Carolina Avenue is delayed; it prevents GPT from assembling a green monopoly once houses become available again.

I am now checking the rent values for my pink properties. St. Charles Place, States Avenue, and Virginia Avenue each cost $140, $140, and $160. Their unimproved rents are $10, $10, and $12.

My four-house pinks would rent $625, $625, and $700. That is strong but weaker than the light blues with four houses, which would rent $400, $400, and $450.
